headline: Wet, windy week; the strongest Pacific storms arrive Friday through Sunday.
summary: A busy Pacific storm track is lining up one storm after another, all fed by a deep low far out over the northeast Pacific. Each system brings rain and strong south winds. A stronger round arrives Tuesday and Wednesday, with gusts of about 40 to 50 mph on the coast and in the north interior, and wind advisories are in effect for those areas. A trio of stronger storms follows from Friday through Sunday. Heavy rain on the coast and the Olympics could push the Skokomish River toward minor flooding, and large swells may bring seas over 20 feet to the coast Friday. Snow levels stay high in the mountains. Forecasters are fairly confident about this week's wind and rain, but the late-week systems are still being refined.
changes: Wind advisories, which earlier discussions called likely or possible, are now in effect for the coast and northern lowlands Tuesday through Wednesday. The Wednesday record-warmth mention from earlier discussions is gone, and the late-week outlook now centers on stronger storms and possible minor flooding on the Skokomish River and at the coast.
